text:
alana (AE): quick heads-up — Acme POC on Dedicated reporting credits burned in ~2h. They say their token meter shows way less. Demo is tomorrow, they're asking for a breakdown and refund of unused credits. can someone triage?

sam (Solutions): looping in support. do we have customer project_id and sample request ids?

alana (AE): project_id: acme-prod-42. customer pasted these request ids from their client logs: r_1a2b3c r_1a2b3d r_1a2b3e — they say each looks like ~1k tokens. we show ~3k total in our portal but they claim 30k.

mia (Support): ok I'll pull usage export and check billing_export. can you drop the request headers they sent? especially x-idempotency-key if present.

alana (AE): they said client has retry loop but thought idempotency key is applied. attaching snippet they sent: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -d '{"prompt":"long prompt...","max_tokens":1024}'` — no idempotency header shown.

sam (Solutions): that could be it. retries without idempotency can create duplicate successful calls if network drop happened before response. mia — can you check if multiple identical responses landed?

mia (Support): checking usage export now. quick note: our portal breaks out "generation_tokens" vs "embedding_units" vs "stream_bytes" — client might be counting characters not tokens.

ops-bot: Alert: cost-alert for acme-prod-42 did NOT fire — threshold configured at $500, current spend $620.

jordan (Finance): FYI credits flow: free credits apply before billed usage. If free credits are exhausted, account starts consuming paid balance. Also our metering counts each completed request call, retries included.

mia (Support): pulled events 2026-03-01T09:02:12Z -> 2026-03-01T11:08:03Z. I see ~18k generation_tokens in the export vs UI summary 3k — looks like duplicates present. Sample rows (sanitized):
```
request_id,runtime_ms,tokens
r_1a2b3c,1200,1024
r_1a2b3c_retry1,1300,1024
r_1a2b3c_retry2,1100,1024
```

sam (Solutions): aha — client retried and server treated each as a new call. do we have idempotency header enforcement?

mia (Support): runtime team confirms we accept idempotency-key header but it's optional; if client doesn't send it we can't dedupe. the SDKs set it by default, looks like Acme used a custom client that didn't.

jordan (Finance): since this is a POC, we can credit back the duplicated spend. need a clear calc: how many duplicate requests and tokens. Mia can you produce a CSV with unique_id + count + duplicated_tokens so I can compute refund amount?

mia (Support): will do. preliminary: ~14 duplicate requests across 3 sessions ~ 13,440 duplicated tokens (generation). I'll export CSV and share in a sec.

alana (AE): please also flag to Project team before tomorrow's demo. customer is anxious. can we offer a short-term mitigation (rate limit/retry window) while they patch client?

sam (Solutions): short-term options: 1) enforce server-side idempotency for any request with same payload + client ip within a 30s window (fast but might block valid replays), 2) ask customer to upgrade to our SDK which includes idempotency keys, 3) issue temporary quota to limit burst. recommend #3 + #2.

mia (Support): created ticket S-2026-1143 and attached usage CSV. Jordan — added estimated refund: 13,440 tokens * $0.00002 = $0.2688 — but our pricing tiers and rounding mean refund will show as $0.27. Also free credits already applied, so net owed credit change = +$0.27 to their account.

jordan (Finance): good. I'll manually apply a credit and update billing record. also setting cost-alert threshold to $400 for acme-prod-42 so ops-bot notifies earlier.

ops-bot: Alert config updated for acme-prod-42 by jordan (Finance) — threshold now $400.

sam (Solutions): to avoid future confusion, I'll draft a note for the customer explaining: why tokens differed (retries), how we count, how free credits applied, and how to enable idempotency in their client. alana, want me to join the call tomorrow?

alana (AE): please do. also add a quick checklist for the demo: (1) confirm SDK idempotency present, (2) patch their retry logic, (3) verify rate limits, (4) confirm credits remaining.

mia (Support): CSV uploaded to the ticket: `acme-prod-42-usage-dup.csv` and support ticket link: https://redwood.internal/tickets/S-2026-1143

alana (AE): customer replied: "thanks — please also explain why portal showed 3k earlier" — Sam, can you add a short explainer about portal aggregation vs raw export?

sam (Solutions): short explainer: UI shows deduped, recent-summary view for quick reading (may apply aggregation windows and hide retry rows), raw export is per-request and shows every completed call. portal summary is intended for billing accuracy over longer windows, but export is the source-of-truth for incident triage. we'll clarify wording in docs.

jordan (Finance): refund applied and credit balance updated. I'll send a confirmation email to Acme after you sign off on numbers, Alana.

alana (AE): thanks team — moving to resolve. Sam pls join demo at 10am PST. Mia, close S-2026-1143 once refund confirmation sent. :thumbsup:

mia (Support): will do, marking as in-progress.

alana (AE): closing note — main blocker was client-side retries without idempotency and misread token counts. lessons: educate POC customers about idempotency, add small UI hint about "exports show raw calls" vs summary.

sam (Solutions): adding a short POC checklist to sales playbook after this.

mia (Support): ticket closed after confirmation email sent.

alana (AE): thread resolved, thanks everyone!"
